title: How do batches overlap without violating dependencies?
scope: The original Read → Prep → Train dependency is preserved for every batch. States are logical snapshots, not measured durations; the full original timing comparison remains below.

steps.label: Start reading
steps.description: Both schedules initially wait for batch 1 to be read. A batch cannot skip preparation.

steps.label: Prepare batch 1
steps.description: CPU consumes completed read B1. Prefetch independently starts B2 while the accelerator is still waiting.

steps.label: Overlap three stages
steps.description: The pipelined schedule trains B2 while preparing B3 and reading B4. Every batch passed its own preceding stages; these are three different batches.

steps.label: Drain prepared work
steps.description: B3 trains after preparation completes. B4 waits prepared in the host queue; storage no longer needs to run for this finite example.

steps.label: Complete the finite pipeline
steps.description: B4 finishes after the pipeline drains. Overlap removes repeated startup gaps only while delivery and the prepared buffer keep up; it does not accelerate any individual stage.

guard: No invented speedup; logical snapshots supplement the original shared-axis schedules.
